explanation: Athenians thought elections favoured the rich and well known. A stone machine called a kleroterion picked citizens at random, though military generals were still elected.

claims.text: In classical Athens, most public officials were chosen by lot rather than by election.
Athenians regarded election as favouring the wealthy and well known, and selection by lot as more democratic.
The kleroterion, a stone allotment machine, was used to select citizens at random.
Athenian generals (strategoi) were elected rather than chosen by lot.
